content:
Continue the following story in about 500 words. Preserve its quiet, realistic tone and resolve the practical problem through the characters' actions rather than a sudden coincidence.

Mara arrived at the mountain village with a cardboard box of replacement radio parts. The road behind her would close at dusk for repairs, and the next delivery was not scheduled until Thursday. At the clinic, the receptionist showed her a receiver that worked only when someone held its loose cable at an awkward angle. A weather notice was expected that evening.

The village electrician, Tomas, had already checked the power supply. He left a diagram on the desk, marking two joints he suspected, but had been called away to repair a water pump. Mara knew how to assemble the newer radios in her workshop; this older unit had labels worn nearly blank. She laid out her tools and discovered that the replacement connector in her box did not match the one on the receiver.

Outside, a schoolteacher was organizing a walking group for the next morning. She needed the weather notice before deciding whether to cancel. The receptionist offered to call a nearby town, but the telephone line had become unreliable during the afternoon rain. Mara asked for a clean cloth, a desk lamp, and the maintenance notebook. Its last entry was dated eleven years earlier. A folded sheet tucked behind the cover listed the names of three former volunteers, one of whom still lived above the grocery shop.
